body.statement: Deciding whether \(X=0\) is a Beckers actual cause of \(Y=0\) is NP-complete on \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{chain}}\); the budgeted problem remains NP-complete when every edge has cost zero and the budget is zero. NP membership uses the retained graph, alternate full state, and supporting table rows. NP-hardness is by a polynomial reduction from distinct-literal \(3\)-SAT in which shared exogenous selector roots encode one Boolean choice per variable and clause gates lie on the endogenous chain; full-graph reachability legality forces every successful clause input to agree with the selector choice.
body.justification: The restriction shows that endogenous treewidth and domain size cannot parameterize an exact Beckers backend by themselves.
body.gap: EiterLukasiewicz2002Complexity and AleksandrowiczEtAl2014 analyze Halpern--Pearl variants; their reductions do not establish hardness for Beckers deletion legality on a deterministic binary endogenous chain of total indegree four.
body.consumer: The backend can refuse an endogenous-chain fast path when shared exogenous roots create nonforest full incidence.
body.proof_tex:
Membership in NP follows directly from the explicit encoding.  Guess \(H\subseteq G\), the nonactual value of \(X\), a value for every endogenous variable in the alternate state, and one original supporting row for each nonintervened projected-table membership.  Reachability in \(H\) checks \(H\in\mathcal H(G)\).  A scan of every explicitly listed row checks all equalities \(Q_Z^{S_Z}(a_{S_Z})=\{a_Z\}\), and each supplied row checks an alternate membership.  By \texttt{lem:canonical-replay}, these checks are equivalent to a full-setting Beckers simplification and alternate solution.  Exact rational addition and comparison are polynomial in the supplied bit length.  For a singleton candidate, the minimality condition is automatic.  Hence both the unbudgeted and budgeted problems are in NP.

For hardness, reduce from the NP-complete problem in \texttt{lem:three-sat-np-complete}.  Repeated literals may be deleted from a clause, a tautological clause may be discarded, and the empty or constant cases may be sent to fixed instances.  Thus we may assume that the formula has variables \(z_1,\ldots,z_n\), at least one clause, at most three distinct literals per clause, and no tautological clause.

For each \(z_i\), introduce binary exogenous roots \(T_i,F_i\), both actually zero.  Construct the endogenous chain
\[
 X\longrightarrow S_1\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow S_n
 \longrightarrow C_1\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow C_m=Y.
\]
The unintervened table of \(X\) is constantly zero.  If \(p\) is the chain predecessor, define
\[
 S_i(p,T_i,F_i)=
 \begin{cases}
 T_i\wedge F_i,&p=0,\\
 T_i\mathbin\oplus F_i,&p=1.
 \end{cases}
\]
At a clause \(K_j\), use \(T_i\) as the root for a positive occurrence of \(z_i\) and \(F_i\) as the root for a negative occurrence.  If its distinct literal roots are \(\ell_{j1},\ldots,\ell_{jk}\), where \(1\le k\le3\), add their edges to \(C_j\) and set
\[
 C_j(p,\ell_{j1},\ldots,\ell_{jk})
 =p\wedge(\ell_{j1}\vee\cdots\vee\ell_{jk}).
\]
All tables are total, deterministic, and binary.  The all-zero state is a solution.  Selector indegree is three and clause indegree is at most four.  Each displayed parent is genuine: the four selector rows exhibit dependence on each parent, and at a clause one may set \(p=1\) and vary one literal, or set one literal to one and vary \(p\).  The number of rows per constructed table is at most sixteen, so the construction is polynomial and belongs to \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{chain}}\).

We next prove the selector invariant.  In any successful witness, every chain edge is retained and every chain node has alternate value one.  To see this, if a nonintervened node changes from zero, its actual-row equality implies that at least one retained parent changes: otherwise its projected actual row would force output zero.  Exogenous roots are fixed at zero.  Backward iteration from \(Y=1\) must therefore use changed endogenous parents, and the only endogenous route from \(X\) to \(Y\) is the displayed chain.  Hence all its edges are retained and, by binarity, all its node values are one.

At \(S_i\), retaining both root edges fixes \((T_i,F_i)=(0,0)\), so with alternate predecessor one the exclusive-or output is zero; this cannot support \(S_i=1\).  Deleting both root edges violates the actual-row equality, because at actual predecessor zero the completion \((T_i,F_i)=(1,1)\) has conjunction output one.  Deleting exactly one root edge is locally admissible: the other retained root is zero, so the conjunction at actual predecessor zero is always zero.  At alternate predecessor one, assigning one to the deleted coordinate and zero to the retained coordinate makes the exclusive-or one.  Thus exactly one of \(T_i\to S_i\) and \(F_i\to S_i\) is deleted.  Call its root selected, and interpret selection of \(T_i\) as \(z_i=\mathrm{true}\) and selection of \(F_i\) as \(z_i=\mathrm{false}\).

Suppose first that the formula has a satisfying assignment.  Select roots according to it, delete every outgoing edge of every selected root, and retain all other edges.  Every deleted edge has a selected root as tail, and such a root has no retained outgoing edge; hence no deleted edge has a retained alternative path and \(H\in\mathcal H(G)\).  The selector calculation proves its actual-row equality.  At each clause, actual predecessor zero makes the output zero for every completion of deleted literal coordinates, so its actual-row equality also holds.  Intervene with \(X\leftarrow1\) and assign one to every chain node.  At a selector, use local value one for its deleted root coordinate.  Each satisfied clause has at least one selected literal root; that incoming edge was deleted, so a supporting row can set that coordinate to one and makes the clause output one.  All projected memberships hold.  By \texttt{lem:canonical-replay}, this is a Beckers witness changing \(Y\) to one.

Conversely, suppose a witness exists and recover its assignment from the selector invariant.  Since \(C_j=1\) and its retained chain predecessor is one, a supporting row for \(C_j\) must set at least one literal-root coordinate to one.  Exogenous roots themselves remain zero, so the corresponding incoming edge \(r\to C_j\) must be deleted.  If \(r\) were not selected, its edge \(r\to S_i\) would be retained.  All chain edges from \(S_i\) through \(S_n,C_1,\ldots,C_j\) are retained, producing a retained directed path from \(r\) to \(C_j\).  This contradicts legality of the deleted edge \(r\to C_j\).  Therefore every clause has a deleted input from a selected root, which is precisely a literal made true by the recovered assignment.  The formula is satisfiable.

The two constructions are polynomial and preserve yes-instances, proving NP-hardness and hence NP-completeness.  Assigning cost zero to every edge and budget zero leaves the existence question unchanged, so the same reduction proves the budgeted restriction.  The proof uses neither unrestricted certificate counting nor a cost-preserving normalization claim.
